text:
Marta: small docs tidy - metering page still suggests 'requests are billed at the plan level' which is misleading now that we surface token-level attribution. planning a short PR to clarify and add a tiny SDK example + dashboard note.
Leo: yes please. paste the sentence you want to replace and your proposed wording.
Marta: current: 'Requests are billed at the plan level associated with the key.'
Proposed: 'Billing is computed per token. By default tokens inherit the API key's tier; an optional override header can attribute some tokens to a different tier for that request.'
Anika: love the clarity. please add a compact example showing a single billing window with split attribution so readers don't assume whole-window reclassification.
Marta: adding example (will be a one-liner in docs):
```
Billing window 2026-11-01:
- API key (default): standard -> 1,150 tokens
- Requests with X-Redwood-Client-Tier: pro-override -> 275 tokens
Result: 1,150 tokens billed at standard tier, 275 tokens billed at pro-override tier (attributed per token).
```
Leo: tiny editorial: use 'override tier' instead of 'pro-override' and avoid 'overage' unless it's a priced overage. also add migration sentence for header rename (old: X-Plan -> new: X-Redwood-Client-Tier).
Marta: done. adding three tiny SDK snippets (curl/node/python) to show optional header usage.
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Client-Tier: override-enterprise" \
  -d '{"prompt":"Summarize meeting notes"}'
```
```js
await fetch('https://api.redwood.com/v1/completions', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${KEY}`, 'X-Redwood-Client-Tier': 'override-enterprise' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ prompt: 'TL;DR' })
})
```
```python
import requests
headers = { 'Authorization': f'Bearer {KEY}', 'X-Redwood-Client-Tier': 'override-enterprise' }
requests.post('https://api.redwood.com/v1/completions', json={'prompt':'TL;DR'}, headers=headers)
```
Anika: also add a one-sentence clarification about routing fallbacks: 'If a request is routed to a different model variant due to rate limits, billing attribution remains based on the API key or explicit override header unless that header/api-key is changed.' saves a lot of support confusion.
Marta: noted and added. docs-ci-bot flagged a broken sidebar link when I ran link tests locally: /billing/tiers -> 404. suggested replacement /pricing/tiers.
docs-ci-bot: Link check: docs/metering.md has 1 broken link: /billing/tiers (404). Suggest using: /pricing/tiers.
Marta: will update the link and add a small docs-test that asserts /pricing/tiers resolves (so we don't regress). also writing a dashboard caption tweak: 'Attribution breakdown: token counts grouped by tier tag (default vs override)'.
SupportBot: FYI support has seen 3 tickets this month where customers assumed their entire window moved tiers. Clarifying examples + header migration note should reduce churn.
Leo: one more request - keep examples short, don't show full tables. and add a changelog entry in metering.md: 'Clarified token-level attribution and added examples (2026-11-02)'.
Marta: done. opening PR now: https://git.redwood.com/redwood/docs/pull/1212 - includes copy change, three SDK snippets, header migration note, link fix, dashboard caption update, changelog line, and a docs-test. tagging @Leo @Anika for review.
Anika: reviewing shortly. small nit: in the python snippet add a comment that header is optional.
Marta: added comment and pushed. thanks!
Anika: LGTM apart from that tiny note, approving now. :white_check_mark:
Leo: approved too. :thumbsup:
Marta: merging after CI completes. thanks all! :rocket:
